test_cases.title: Every emitted row carries a non-empty program_id (env wins, yaml fallback, unresolved skips write)
test_cases.given: copilot-activity.mjs is asked to assemble Copilot Chat rows and program_id must be resolved from env → .harness/program.yaml → skip
test_cases.when: the row-builder runs for three fixtures — (a) HARNESS_PROGRAM_ID set, (b) unset with .harness/program.yaml present, (c) both absent
test_cases.then: (a)+(b) every appended row in activity.jsonl carries a non-empty program_id matching the resolved source; (c) NDJSON append is skipped and a single program_id_unresolved log line is written — no row with empty/placeholder program_id is ever emitted (the ING-04 141× regression)
test_cases.objective: Guard the ING-04 root cause: every row appended by copilot-activity.mjs to docs/activity/activity.jsonl must carry a non-empty program_id, sourced from HARNESS_PROGRAM_ID env with fallback to .harness/program.yaml (accepting both program_id and legacy programId keys), and the hook must refuse to write rather than emit an empty program_id.
preconditions: Fixture journal streams for kinds 0/1/2 that would normally produce ≥1 row per session-end
Ability to stub process.env and the .harness/program.yaml read path within the test
steps: Case A: set process.env.HARNESS_PROGRAM_ID='prog_env_ING05', unset the .harness/program.yaml fixture, run the row-builder against a fixture that produces ≥1 row, collect the lines appended to activity.jsonl

Case B: unset HARNESS_PROGRAM_ID, provide a .harness/program.yaml fixture with program_id='prog_yaml_ING05' (repeat with legacy programId='prog_yaml_legacy_ING05'), run the row-builder, collect the appended lines
Case C: unset HARNESS_PROGRAM_ID AND provide no .harness/program.yaml, run the row-builder against the same fixture, collect activity.jsonl contents and .mcp-push.log contents
expected_results: Case A: every appended row has row.program_id === 'prog_env_ING05' (non-empty string, no null, no empty string)
Case B: every appended row has row.program_id === 'prog_yaml_ING05' (or 'prog_yaml_legacy_ING05' for the legacy-key variant); env source is preferred when both are present
Case C: activity.jsonl gains ZERO new rows for the session-end; .mcp-push.log gains exactly one JSON line with event='program_id_unresolved'
Across all cases: no row is ever emitted with an empty, null, or placeholder program_id

test_cases.title: MCP push aborts by TIMEOUT_MS on a stalled server; parent hook returns without waiting on the detached child
test_cases.given: harness-mcp-push.mjs is configured with TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000 and fetch is stubbed to never resolve; copilot-activity.mjs spawns the push script detached with stdio:'ignore' and .unref()
test_cases.when: the push script issues the first MCP RPC call and the parent hook completes its NDJSON write and calls spawn(...).unref()
test_cases.then: the AbortController fires and the script exits by ≤ 10.5 s wall-clock with exactly one 'timeout' log line and zero retry attempts, AND the parent copilot-activity.mjs process returns without awaiting the child (child.unref() called; no ipc/stdout wait)
test_cases.objective: Prove the fire-and-forget contract (AC-2) and the single-attempt timeout discipline (FR-5): a stalled MCP server cannot hang the Copilot Chat Stop event, and the push script never retries.
preconditions: Node 20+ test runner (node:test) with fake timers or real 11 s tolerance
fetch is stubbed at the module boundary to return a Promise that never resolves (or resolves only after 30 s)
spawn is stubbed/observable so the test can assert options.detached === true, options.stdio === 'ignore', and child.unref was called
steps: Stub global fetch to return a Promise that never resolves; import harness-mcp-push.mjs and invoke its entrypoint against the default URL
Start a monotonic timer immediately before the invocation; await process exit
Read the lines appended to docs/activity/.mcp-push.log during the run

Separately, stub spawn in copilot-activity.mjs's module boundary, invoke the parent entrypoint end-to-end against a row-producing fixture, and capture the spawn call arguments plus whether the returned ChildProcess had .unref() invoked
Assert the parent entrypoint's returned promise resolves without awaiting the (fake) child
expected_results: The push script exits within 10.5 s of invocation (wall-clock ≤ TIMEOUT_MS + 500 ms tolerance)
docs/activity/.mcp-push.log gains exactly one JSON line with event='timeout' and duration_ms ≈ 10000
fetch was called exactly once (no second initialize attempt, no retry loop)
spawn was called with options.detached === true and options.stdio === 'ignore'
child.unref() was invoked before the parent's entrypoint returned
The parent entrypoint resolves without a completion signal from the child

test_cases.title: Push failures (network error / non-2xx / timeout) write exactly one .mcp-push.log line and exit code 0
test_cases.given: harness-mcp-push.mjs is invoked against a fetch stub that yields one of three failure modes — connection refused (network error), 503 response (non-2xx), or a hang past TIMEOUT_MS (timeout)
test_cases.when: the script finishes handling each failure mode
test_cases.then: docs/activity/.mcp-push.log gains exactly one JSON line per invocation describing the outcome, the process exits with code 0, and no exception propagates back to the Copilot Chat hook that spawned it
test_cases.objective: Verify best-effort observability (AC-5, NFR-observability): every push failure produces exactly one grep-parseable log line under the field allowlist and NEVER surfaces as a non-zero exit or thrown error to the parent hook.
preconditions: Node 20+ test runner with the ability to stub global fetch per test case
docs/activity/.mcp-push.log is empty (or a temp path is substituted) at the start of each sub-case
process.exit is stubbed to capture the exit code without terminating the test process
steps: For each sub-case in test_data.sub_cases: reset the log file, install the corresponding fetch stub, invoke the harness-mcp-push.mjs entrypoint
After each invocation, read the log file contents, split by newline, and JSON.parse each non-empty line
Capture the exit code recorded by the stubbed process.exit
Inspect the parsed log object for the presence of allowlisted fields and the absence of forbidden fields
expected_results: Each sub-case appends exactly one line to docs/activity/.mcp-push.log — no more, no fewer
The parsed log object's event field equals the sub-case's expected_event ('network_error' | 'http_error' | 'timeout')
The stubbed process.exit is called with code 0 in every sub-case
No exception propagates out of the entrypoint in any sub-case (parent hook sees a clean detached-child exit)
Every logged object contains only fields from log_field_allowlist; none of the forbidden_log_fields appears anywhere in the line

notes: Deliberate 3-TC cap per user request; uncovered ids are expected and will be surfaced at the Phase 4 Product Gate for approval.
ING-05-NFR-accessibility is N/A (background Node hook, no UI surface — PRD § Non-functional requirements).

TC-02 is anchored to FR-5 (the observable being asserted with the stalled fetch stub) but also covers AC-2's non-blocking spawn assertion and NFR-performance's 10 s per-call bound in-line (steps + expected_results).
TC-03 covers NFR-observability's bounded-log-line + field-allowlist contract as part of the AC-5 assertion body.
